concept.title: Clubs, groups and social activities
concept.shortdesc: Joining clubs, performing arts, music, reading and social groups, children's and youth sessions, and informal get-togethers for fun and meeting people.

conbody.note: Draft group. Groups are a convenience for browsing the draft: the hierarchy was proposed by a second clustering pass and named by a language model, and no person has reviewed it.

ul.li: : Keeping in touch or joining group conversations remotely by video call, phone, messaging or webchat.
: Taking part in amateur drama, musical theatre, dance and other performing arts sessions, rehearsals and performances, with some disco and DJ activities.
: Taking part in singing, whether in a choir, community singing group or informal singing session.
: Going to watch live music, comedy, shows and other entertainment as an audience member.
: Learning or playing musical instruments and making music with others in classes, workshops, bands and music clubs.
: Meeting to read and discuss books together, including shared reading groups and related writing groups.
: Sessions for young children and families with stories, nursery rhymes, songs and shared books.
: Clubs and playschemes for children running in school holidays with games, crafts, sports and outdoor activities.
: Clubs for school-age children held after the school day, including sports, arts, STEM and homework clubs.
: General sessions of fun, creative or themed activities and games for socialising, with no single named activity as the focus.
: Regular club or group sessions for children and young people, with games, activities and peer company.
: Informal sessions that people can attend without booking to get support, advice, information or a welcome, including some Q&A and volunteer sessions.
: Joining or attending clubs, interest groups and group sessions where the type of activity is generic or varied.
: Attending or running workshops, practical demonstrations and short taught sessions on a topic of interest.
: Attending regular, usually monthly, meetings or meet-ups of a club, society or social group.
: Casual time together with friends and family, hanging out, chatting and catching up without a set activity.
: Groups and gatherings whose aim is meeting new people, forming friendships and building confidence or skills alongside.
: Borrowing, browsing or reading books, audiobooks, magazines, newspapers and similar items from a library or lending collection.
